newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea seen shipping 10,000T copper to Singapore.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea seen shipping 10,000T copper to Singapore.

text.p: A cargo of 10,000 tonnes of copper is reported to be sitting in South Korea's southeastern port of Pusan awaiting shipment to Singapore at the end of June or early July, Asian metal dealers said on Thursday.
They said the copper belonged to LG Metals Corp, South Korea's largest copper producer and an affiliate of LG Group, although a company spokesman declined to comment on its physical metal business.
"There are rumours some 10,000 tonnes of South Korean copper is moving to Singapore at the end of June or early July. People are watching this," a Tokyo-based metals dealer said.

He said it was not surprising that copper is being shipped to the London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouse in Singapore as U.S. Commodity Exchange (COMEX) copper prices are around $80 a tonne lower than LME quotes.
"The arrival in Singapore is set for the second week of July," another trade source said, adding the copper was believed to have been sold to a European LME ring dealing member.

Some traders in Seoul said the current slump in South Korean base metals demand, caused by an economic slowdown after a series of corporate collapses, has forced LG Metals to ship its copper stocks overseas.
Other traders said the shipment could be aimed at covering LG Metals' short copper positions on the LME or is just a commercial trade.

Earlier this month an LG Metals spokesman said the metals market had "no need to worry" about its current open LME metal options positions, but declined to comment on rumours in London the firm was facing huge losses after a copper rally in early June.
Copper prices staged a mini-rally during late Wednesday LME trading, although the market still closed easier after hitting seven-week lows earlier.
Traders attributed copper's latest losses to another wave of speculative selling, sell-stops, and option-related sales.
Short-term fundamentals remain supportive, however, and the cash/threes backwardation, which wobbled at one stage, still ended over $100.
Copper's low-point was $2,355, which at that stage was over nine percent below the highs near $2,600 that prevailed only last Friday.

Later on Wednesday on the COMEX market in New York, copper ended sharply lower, the industrial metal succumbing to further selling despite the big drop Tuesday which some believe was already overdone.
